## [0.6.2] - 2026-08-25

### Added

- Attendee detail's wallet "More actions" menu has a new "Refresh status" action - pulls the pass's current device-registration status directly from the provider on demand, instead of waiting for the periodic background sync to reach that one attendee (which can take up to 30 minutes, longer if many other passes are stale system-wide). For when the provider's own dashboard already shows a pass as added but Admitto hasn't caught up yet. Shares the same rate limit as the other single-attendee wallet actions (void/restore/reissue/delete), since it also calls the provider once per request. A momentary "not found" from the provider (the same brief search-index lag the duplicate-recovery fix above already accounts for) is retried once rather than taken as final, so it can't wipe a genuinely-registered pass's status back to unregistered.
- An unhandled promise rejection or an exception thrown outside a request's normal error handling is now logged (to System logs and stdout) with enough detail to diagnose before the process exits, instead of only ever surfacing as a bare Node.js stack trace in the container's raw logs.

### Changed

- The staff admin/operator app's build no longer ships the full timezone database (used for the timezone picker and timezone-abbreviation display) bundled into its main entry script - it now loads as its own separate file. This was pushing the entry script past Vite's 500 kB chunk-size warning and slowing down first paint with data most visits never touch; it now downloads in parallel and, since it only changes when the timezone-data dependency itself is upgraded, browsers can keep reusing their cached copy across app deploys instead of re-downloading it every time.
- Check-in's camera QR scanner now asks the decoder to try harder on a difficult frame instead of moving on after one pass, which should make it lock onto a skewed, low-contrast, or partially obscured ticket QR code more reliably (at the cost of a slightly slower decode per frame). Applies identically on every device/browser, unlike focus and zoom, which only some cameras support.

### Fixed

- Picking a venue from the location search while creating a new event now saves its full structured address (object name, street, postal code, city, region, country) along with the map pin, instead of only the pin and formatted address - previously those structured fields stayed empty until an admin reselected the same venue afterward on the event's Location settings tab, which is where they were actually being saved.
- Event Settings → Ticket types' small color/name preview badge next to a ticket type's name field now updates live as the admin types, instead of staying on the previous name until the field lost focus - which most admins only discovered by tabbing away or by pressing Enter, with no indication that either was needed.
- An attendee's "Ticket link copied" activity log entry produced by opening "View sent message" now records the operator's own timezone instead of falling back to the event's timezone, matching every other activity log row - previously it could show a visibly different UTC offset than the operator's other actions on the same attendee if the event's own timezone differed from the operator's.
- Communication's Delivery details modal, and its "Export as .txt" timeline, no longer show a stale error message (for example "Connection timeout") for a delivery that went out on a later automatic retry - the error notice, and each exported timeline row's error text, now only appear when that delivery's current status is itself a failure (failed, bounced, rejected), instead of surfacing left-over error text from an earlier failed attempt on the same row alongside a "Sent" status.
- Adding a pass to Apple/Google Wallet for the first time no longer occasionally shows a "?walletError=1" retry banner when PassCreator's create-duplicate check and its own search index briefly disagree (create says the pass already exists, search finds nothing yet) - one retry after a short delay now covers that lag.
- Clicking "Add to Wallet" for the same attendee from two devices at nearly the same time (e.g. a work computer and a phone, before either had created the pass yet) could mint two separate passes at PassCreator instead of one - the second one silently orphaned, invisible to any later Push updates/void/delete, since Admitto had no record of it. The two requests now share one in-flight creation instead of racing.
- The public ticket page, QR image, and static map endpoints now allow far more requests per minute from the same apparent IP address before throttling (60 to 500). A single public IP can represent many unrelated attendees at once - most commonly behind a shared corporate network, or behind a mobile carrier's large-scale NAT, which is common in some regions and can put hundreds of distinct subscribers behind one address simultaneously - and the previous limit could show a legitimate attendee a "Too Many Requests" error for opening their own ticket link.
- Single-attendee wallet actions (void, restore, reissue, delete) allowed only 10 requests every 10 minutes per admin and event, which could interrupt an admin correcting several attendees' passes back to back. The limit is now 10 requests per minute instead - PassCreator's own outbound call pacing (see Security below) is now the layer actually protecting against exceeding PassCreator's rate limit, so this route's limit can bound scripted abuse rather than ordinary manual corrections.
- Bulk wallet actions on a whole selection (void, reissue, delete), and bulk-delete/bulk-revoke-pass on a wallet-configured event, allowed only 3 requests every 10 minutes per admin and event - tight enough that an admin working through a large event in batches of 100 attendees had to wait between almost every batch. The limit is now 10 requests every 10 minutes, for the same reason as above: PassCreator's outbound pacing, not this HTTP-level limit, is what actually bounds provider traffic.
- A delivery whose first attempt failed (for example an SMTP connection timeout) and then succeeded on a later automatic or manual retry now has its stored error message and error code cleared, instead of keeping the earlier failure's text in the database indefinitely next to the now-successful status.
- `apps/admin`'s full test suite (`npx vitest run`) would intermittently fail 7-14 of its 264 files with `Test timed out in 5000ms`, a different random set each run, on developer machines with many CPU cores - Vitest's default worker count (`availableParallelism() - 1`) spun up enough concurrent jsdom/React environments to starve individual tests of CPU time under load. Worker concurrency is now capped and the per-test timeout raised as a second line of defense; every flagged test already passed reliably in isolation, confirming this was resource contention, not a real timing bug.
- The event Overview page's Recent activity feed, and the check-in camera's "Already checked in" timestamp, now show each entry in the timezone the acting admin's browser reported at the time it happened (falling back to the current viewer's own browser timezone when that wasn't captured), instead of always showing the event's own timezone - previously, an admin working from a different timezone than the event's venue saw every activity timestamp offset to the venue's zone instead of their own, for example seeing India's UTC+5:30 while working from Europe.

### Security

- The public ticket page, the staff admin/operator app, and every sign-in or account-security page (login, two-factor, forced password change, single sign-on linking) now tell browsers to always use HTTPS for this site, the same protection the API already had. Previously that only reached these pages through Admitto's own bundled reverse proxy; a deployment that skips it (for example, the documented Portainer/NAS setup without the bundled nginx) shipped the public ticket page - which loads no scripts of its own, so it had no other way to pick this up - with no such protection at all.
- The staff admin/operator app now tells browsers that only it, and nothing else, may ever use the device camera (needed for check-in QR scanning), and denies every other sensitive device feature (microphone, location, and more) outright; the public ticket page and every sign-in/account page now deny all of those, since none of them use any.
- Fixed a reverse-proxy/app mismatch where the bundled nginx layer stamped a fixed referrer-handling value onto every response, silently overriding the stricter value the public ticket page sets for itself (send no referrer information anywhere) whenever nginx sits in front of the app. This wasn't exploitable in practice, since nothing sensitive travels in a ticket link, but the app's own per-page choice is now always the one that reaches the browser.
- Settings → External services → Maps' custom tile URL is now checked for a private, loopback, link-local, or cloud-metadata host at save time, the same check its Geocoding base URL and the Weather base URL fields already get - previously a tile URL pointing at one of those would save successfully and only fail once the map itself tried to render.
- The bundled nginx reverse-proxy config (`deploy/nginx/default.conf`) no longer reports its own version in the `Server` response header or on its default error pages.
- `deploy/docker-entrypoint.sh`'s root-only fallback path (never used by the shipped image, which always drops to the unprivileged `node` user before this script runs) no longer rebuilds a shell command string from its arguments - a follow-up command containing a literal `$(...)` could have been re-evaluated by that fallback's shell instead of passed through as plain text.
- The attendee list's bulk actions (delete, check-in, revoke check-in, revoke items, revoke pass, change ticket type, change RSVP status) and every wallet action that calls Apple/Google Wallet's provider (void, restore, reissue, delete - both for one attendee and for a whole selection) now have a rate limit, matching the protection already in place for bulk email sends and single-attendee edits. Previously an admin account, or a compromised admin session, could resend the same bulk-delete or wallet-void request in a tight loop with no limit - bulk-delete in particular has no undo. Every one of the bulk (whole-selection) requests among these is also now capped at a generous size (well past what selecting hundreds of attendees ever needs), closing off an oversized request as a way to waste server resources before it's even processed.
- Wallet actions that act on a whole selection at once (void, reissue, delete) now have a much tighter rate limit of their own, separate from the single-attendee one above - each of these already calls PassCreator once per selected attendee, so sharing the single-attendee limit would still have allowed far more PassCreator calls in a burst than PassCreator's own rate limit allows.
- Bulk-deleting attendees, or bulk-revoking their passes, now shares that same tighter wallet-action rate limit too, in addition to the general bulk-action one - both can also call PassCreator once per selected attendee (for anyone in the selection who has a wallet pass), which the general bulk-action limit alone didn't account for.
- Every call Admitto makes to PassCreator, from any action (single, bulk, or a background wallet sync/push job), is now paced to a steady rate instead of firing as many at once as the calling code allows - closes a gap where the rate limits above bounded how many bulk actions an admin could start, but not how fast the resulting PassCreator calls actually went out, which could still burst past PassCreator's own limit and leave part of a large bulk action failed. A bulk action against a large selection now takes noticeably longer to finish, instead of appearing to complete quickly while quietly failing for some of the selection. This pacing is now coordinated across every server process handling requests, not just within one - previously, running more than one process could let the combined rate of outbound PassCreator calls exceed the intended pace even though each process individually stayed within it.
- Bulk wallet actions on a whole selection (void, reissue, delete) now accept at most 100 attendees per request, down from the general bulk-action limit of 500 - since these calls PassCreator once per selected attendee at the steady pace above, a full-size request under the old limit could take long enough to outlive a typical reverse proxy's response timeout even though it was still working correctly in the background. Self-hosted deployments using the bundled nginx config also get a longer read timeout for these specific routes, as defense in depth.
- Bulk-deleting attendees or bulk-revoking their passes on an event that has Wallet configured is now held to that same 100-attendee cap - both can also call PassCreator once per selected attendee, so a large selection on a wallet-enabled event was exposed to the same slow-request risk the dedicated wallet actions above were already capped for. An event with no Wallet configured is unaffected and keeps the general 500-attendee limit, since neither route can reach PassCreator at all in that case.
- Every rate limit backed by Redis (login, MFA, wallet actions, public ticket/QR routes, and every other limit in the app) now falls back to a per-process in-memory limiter that still enforces the configured limit when Redis becomes unreachable, instead of allowing unlimited traffic for the rest of the outage. A single-instance deployment keeps its full protection during a Redis outage; a multi-instance deployment degrades to per-replica protection instead of losing rate limiting entirely.
- The two-factor recovery-code verification limit is now 10 attempts per 15 minutes, down from 30 - matching the TOTP and WebAuthn step-up limits already in place. A legitimate sign-in never needs more than a handful of attempts against the small set of one-time recovery codes issued at enrollment.
- Bulk wallet actions on a whole selection (void, reissue, delete) now also cap how many can run at the same time for one admin and event, not just how many can start in a 10-minute window - previously, a handful of these fired concurrently (for example a double-click, or a browser resending the same request) could queue enough outbound PassCreator calls onto the shared, paced connection that the last one in the queue outlived the reverse proxy's response timeout, showing the admin a failure while the mutations kept running server-side. Submitting one batch, waiting for it to finish, then submitting the next is unaffected.
- Template test-send and both mail transport test routes (organization and event level) now each have a second, hourly limit on top of their existing per-minute one, so leaving the button pressed no longer sends far more test mail in an hour than any real template-editing or transport-diagnosis session needs. The organization and event-level transport test routes also tightened their per-minute limit from 5 to 3, since each dials a real SMTP/Graph connection rather than rendering a template. All three routes now additionally share one instance-wide limit per recipient address (5 per hour, regardless of which route, event, or admin account sends it) - closing a gap where a compromised admin session could send far more test mail to one external address than any single route's own limit implies, by switching between routes, events, or accounts. That per-recipient limit is enforced without ever storing the address itself as part of the rate-limit bucket - only a keyed hash of it, so the address does not show up as plain text in Redis inspection tools, monitoring, snapshots, or backups.
- The SMTP/Graph connectivity probe (both organization and event level) and the event-level bounce-ingest connectivity test and manual run no longer share a rate limit with the actual test-send routes above - previously, running a handful of any combination of these unrelated diagnostics could exhaust the hourly budget meant for test emails and block an admin from sending any, or vice versa.

---

### Deploy
- Container image: `ghcr.io/solarssk/admitto:0.6.2` (rolling `:0.6`)
- Migrations apply **automatically on container start**. **No manual `migrate deploy`.** Back up the database yourself before upgrading (the stack no longer takes an automatic pre-migration backup).

[Full changelog](https://github.com/solarssk/admitto/blob/v0.6.2/CHANGELOG.md)
